clue.text: One activity which has dispensed with the machine

definitions.text: One activity which has dispensed with the machine

parts.words: One activity which has dispensed with the machine
parts.note: the machine is the old wheeled bathing hut that carried swimmers into the shallows; the pastime of a dip in the waves now goes on without it

explanation.surface: Some modern pursuit that no longer needs its machinery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The machine' sounds industrial, but it is the Victorian bathing machine, a hut on wheels that was rolled into the waves so bathers could undress and enter unseen.
explanation.definitionFit: Swimming in the ocean is a leisure activity once done from bathing machines, which have long since gone.

clue.text: Was perhaps Member for. Slough

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the word was might be differently arranged

parts.note: MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A man who may once have sat in Parliament for the Berkshire town of Slough.
explanation.walkthrough: Slough is a town west of London, so 'Member for Slough' reads as its MP; but slough is also a bog. 'Perhaps' rearranges WAS to SWA.
explanation.definitionFit: A slough is a muddy bog or marsh, a synonym of the wet ground meant.

clue.text: Browning had a version of this Greek king

parts.words: Browning had a version of this Greek king
parts.note: the poet Robert Browning published an English translation of the Aeschylus tragedy named after the leader of the Greeks at Troy

explanation.surface: A Victorian poet's take on an ancient monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Browning' might suggest a gun or cooking, but it is Robert Browning, whose 1877 translation of Aeschylus's play bears the king's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The king of Mycenae who led the Greek army against Troy.

clue.text: Sort of see how a charcoal pipe is made

indicators.note: how a thing is made means its letters are formed, so the words are rearranged into a new word

explanation.surface: A craftsman explaining how a briar pipe of charcoal is manufactured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is the jurisdiction of a bishop, not the verb; the adjective describes an archbishop's. The letters of CHARCOAL PIPE IS rearrange to make it.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to an archbishop, so an archbishop's diocese is this sort of ecclesiastical district.

clue.text: In a tangle likely to fuse the grass-drier?

parts.note: hay is grass cut and dried, here pictured as the product of a drier
wire in an electrical fuse is what melts, so fuse wire is likely to fuse

explanation.surface: A tangled farm machine for drying grass that may blow a fuse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fuse' suggests an electrical fault, and fuse wire is the part that melts.
explanation.definitionFit: Gone haywire means chaotic or out of control, like baling wire snarled up.

clue.text: Named to give wartime shipping the all-clear one way

definitions.note: an adjective for the person named; the answer is the noun for that person

parts.note: telling ships in war there is no mine ahead is the all-clear
E is east, one of the compass directions or ways

explanation.surface: A naval officer signalling that the sea lanes are safe in one direction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One way' suggests a single direction of the all-clear, but it is E, east.
explanation.definitionFit: A person put forward or appointed by name for a post or award.

clue.text: The century in toto needs taking off

definitions.note: describes froth or dirt that must be skimmed from a surface; a noun phrase for the thing removed

indicators.note: the Latin phrase supplies the word in, read as putting one piece inside another

parts.note: toto is Latin for total, and a total is a sum
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a century

explanation.surface: A Latin tag about a hundred years in their entirety being removed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In toto' looks like a single Latin phrase meaning 'altogether', but it splits: 'in' puts C inside SUM, a word for total.
explanation.definitionFit: Froth and impurities on a liquid's surface are skimmed away, so they are what needs removing.

clue.text: He'll chew up all comers?

parts.note: chew is the verb to munch noisily, and a winner who defeats every challenger is one who beats all comers

explanation.walkthrough: The word means to munch noisily, and is also short for a champion who beats all challengers.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for champion, a winner who beats every challenger, and also a verb for munching.

clue.text: To see how they're shaping watch them at work

definitions.text: To see how they're shaping watch them at work

parts.words: To see how they're shaping watch them at work
parts.note: shaping means both progressing and literally forming things, as sculptors in clay do

explanation.walkthrough: 'How they're shaping' sounds like 'how they are getting on', but these people literally shape things.
explanation.definitionFit: People who sculpt or build scale figures and replicas are literally shaping things.

clue.text: Fast Nato vessel to shadow shipping ?

parts.note: flying means moving fast
the Netherlands is a Nato member, and a Dutchman is a Dutch ship

explanation.surface: A fast allied warship sent to follow merchant vessels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shadow' looks like a verb for tailing, but describes a phantom: the legendary ghost ship that haunts sailors.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary phantom ship doomed to sail forever, a spectral presence haunting other vessels.

clue.text: Blubber away ?

parts.note: read as a weep heard from a long distance off, a sob some way away

explanation.walkthrough: 'Blubber' suggests whale fat, but here it is the verb to weep; a weep in the distance is the phrase meaning something very different.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means a long distance or a great difference, and literally pictures a weeping sound heard from afar.

clue.text: Duck does not go well with hog's fat

parts.note: mal is the French and prefix form for badly, things that do not go well
lard is rendered pig fat

explanation.surface: A diner complaining that a bird dish clashes with pork dripping.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a food pairing; in fact MAL- (as in malfunction) means badly.
explanation.definitionFit: The commonest wild species of dabbling water bird, the green-headed drake being familiar.

clue.text: Forward-looking TV ?

parts.note: TV taken as the vision part of television, with forward meaning beforehand: sight ahead of time

explanation.walkthrough: TV stands for vision, and 'forward-looking' supplies the prefix meaning before, giving sight of things to come.
explanation.definitionFit: Foresight, seeing events in advance, is literally sight ahead of time.

clue.text: Push one Member to back the French

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
MP is a Member of Parliament

indicators.note: back used as a verb means to turn round, so the French article is written backwards

parts.note: le is the French masculine word for the

explanation.surface: Urging a single politician to support France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To back' reads as 'to support', the surface's politics, but it is the reversal signal on the French article.
explanation.definitionFit: To drive or urge forward is to propel, a synonym of push.

clue.text: Time to get junior out of bed, say ?

indicators.note: say signals that the words are as spoken, sounding like the entry

parts.note: a son, the junior of the family, is up when out of bed

explanation.surface: A parent wondering when to rouse the youngest child in the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Son up' (the junior out of bed) sounds like the dawn hour; 'to get' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: Dawn is the time of day when daylight appears over the horizon.

clue.text: Put on the list for the way he cuddles

indicators.note: the way he does something suggests the manner, so the words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Booking a slot for a man's style of hugging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The way he cuddles' signals an anagram of HE CUDDLES.
explanation.definitionFit: To be listed in a timetable or programme is to be planned for a set time.

clue.text: Always space among trees in a 1 down

definitions.note: the cross-reference points to the answer at 1 down, a marsh or slough

parts.note: ever means always, as in ever hopeful
a glade is an open clearing in a wood

explanation.surface: A clearing in the woods that is forever found within a marsh.
explanation.walkthrough: The OCR lost the '1' of '1 down', the cross-reference to the marsh at 1 down. Florida's famous marshland takes this name.
explanation.definitionFit: A marshy tract of land with tall grass, as in the Florida wetlands, is a kind of swamp.

clue.text: What a sight is the peacock's tail!

definitions.text: What a sight is the peacock's tail

parts.words: What a sight is the peacock's tail
parts.note: in myth Hera set the hundred eyes of the giant Argus in the peacock's tail, so the tail has eyes all over

explanation.walkthrough: 'What a sight' sounds like admiration, but sight is eyesight: the peacock's tail carries the many eyes of the giant Argus.
explanation.definitionFit: Watchful and keen-sighted, like the hundred-eyed giant whose eyes Hera placed on the peacock's tail.

clue.text: Weapon for manual employees

parts.note: manual means done by hand
a staff is the employees of a firm

explanation.surface: Arms supplied for workers who do things by hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Manual employees' reads as labourers, but splits into two words; the result is an old weapon, a staff wielded in the hand.
explanation.definitionFit: An old weapon, a javelin or quarterstaff held in the fist.

clue.text: Al is at a dog's home

definitions.text: Al is at a dog's home

parts.words: Al is at a dog's home
parts.note: the home of the wolfish German shepherd breed is taken as Alsace, its old Latin name, and the opening words nearly spell it

explanation.surface: A man called Al visiting a kennels.
explanation.walkthrough: The name is the Latin for Alsace, home of the breed called after it, and also old slang for the Whitefriars sanctuary in London.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin name of Alsace, which gave its name to the dog breed also called the German shepherd.

clue.text: A stirring of the firs, lad

definitions.text: A stirring of the firs, lad

indicators.note: stirring means moving about, so the letters of the trees' name are shuffled

parts.note: a son is a lad

explanation.surface: Someone telling a boy about a rustle running through the pine trees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stirring' mixes the letters of FIRS, followed by SON for lad; the whole clue also pictures a thrilling shiver through the trees.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden thrill or shiver of excitement, a stirring of the emotions.

clue.text: Advocates in the Hamburg espionage case

indicators.note: in signals that the letters are found within the words of the German spy case

explanation.surface: Lawyers handling a German spying trial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Advocates' and 'case' suggest lawyers in court; the answer is the verb, sitting across 'HambURG ESpionage'.
explanation.definitionFit: To advocate is to recommend or press for something, which is what one who pleads strongly does.

clue.text: How to lie and tell a pet not to

parts.note: a dog is a household pet
telling the pet not to lie down is ordering it to go

explanation.surface: Instructions for lying down, and for stopping a pet from doing so.
explanation.walkthrough: To lie 'doggo' is to keep still and hidden; the wordplay is the command 'Dog, go!', the opposite of telling it to lie.
explanation.definitionFit: Lying doggo is lying low, quiet and unnoticed, the manner in which one hides.

clue.text: Like their namesake, become expansive when there's a drop of wet

definitions.text: Like their namesake, become expansive when there's a drop of wet

parts.words: Like their namesake, become expansive when there's a drop of wet
parts.note: the large umbrellas are named after Sarah Gamp in Dickens, who carried one and grew expansive with a drink

explanation.walkthrough: Mrs Gamp, Dickens's nurse in Martin Chuzzlewit, carried a big umbrella and liked a drop of gin; the umbrellas named after her open out in rain.
explanation.definitionFit: Large untidy umbrellas, named after the Dickens character who carried one.

clue.text: Such wearing litigation for tourists ?

parts.note: read as luggage boxes holding the clothes one wears, and as court actions, litigation, both carried by travellers

explanation.walkthrough: 'Wearing' sounds like tiresome, but it means clothing to wear; the same word for an outfit also names a lawsuit, so the luggage puns on litigation.
explanation.definitionFit: Travellers carry their clothes in these luggage boxes, which also pun on court suits.

clue.text: Bacon taken by partisans

explanation.surface: Rashers served to political supporters.
explanation.definitionFit: Bacon comes in whole flitches cut from the pig's flank, and partisans each take a position in a dispute.

clue.text: Elia canonized — can you beat that ?

parts.note: Elia was the pen name of the essayist Charles Lamb
canonized means made a saint, shown as A ST

explanation.surface: Praising an essayist made a saint and asking if anything could top it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can you beat that?' looks like amazement, but beat means thrash, the definition. LAMB is Charles Lamb, who wrote as Elia; canonized gives A ST, a saint.
explanation.definitionFit: To lambast is to thrash or berate severely, so the question asks for a verb of beating.

clue.text: South to a Chinese port goes Edward, and dog

parts.note: Amoy is the old name for the Chinese port now called Xiamen
Ed is short for Edward

explanation.surface: Edward travelling south to China with his dog.
explanation.walkthrough: Amoy is the older Western name for Xiamen in Fujian.
explanation.definitionFit: A white Siberian breed of sled hound with a thick coat.

clue.text: Delta river at sundown ?

parts.note: D is Delta in the phonetic alphabet
the Usk is a river in Wales

explanation.surface: Arriving at a river mouth as the sun sets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Delta' suggests a river mouth but is only the letter D; the Usk flows through South Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Twilight, the darkening after the sun sets, is evening's start.

clue.text: Delivered by Cossack commanders against Belgrade

definitions.text: Delivered by Cossack commanders against Belgrade

parts.words: Delivered by Cossack commanders against Belgrade
parts.note: describes the artillery bombardments a besieging Russian army would fire at the Serbian city

explanation.walkthrough: The scene is a siege: what commanders deliver against a city's walls is a barrage of heavy gunfire.
explanation.definitionFit: A sustained bombardment by heavy guns, the kind an attacking army fires at a besieged town.
